disease_label_per_paper: The leukemoid reaction in severe alcoholic hepatitis
presentation_summary: 35-year-old man with a 10-year chronic alcohol history presented with two episodes of blood in stool, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite for three days.
He was conscious and oriented with BP 120/70 mmHg, pulse 88/min, respiratory rate 16/min, jaundice/icterus, and tender hepatomegaly 2 cm below the right costal margin.

Admission labs showed hemoglobin 9 g/dL, total leukocyte count 68,000/cumm, neutrophils 50%, bands 20%, total bilirubin 18.2 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 12.4 mg/dL, CRP 22 mg/dL, AST 390 U/L, ALT 152 U/L, PT 19 seconds, and severe alcoholic hepatitis scores including MDF 48 and MELD 20.
Culture negativity, JAK2 negativity, peripheral smear interpretation, steroid response, and final leukemoid-reaction attribution are kept as confirmatory/non-ranking.

outcome.source_text_value: bilirubin came down to 4 mg/dL; TLC 16,000 at discharge and 8,500 after one-month follow-up

quality_warnings: Marked leukocytosis, bandemia, GI bleeding, and CRP are preserved as rankable presentation evidence because they were present at admission.
Culture negativity, JAK2 testing, peripheral smear adjudication, steroid response, and final attribution are confirmatory/non-ranking.
This case pressures the manifold to represent leukemoid alcoholic hepatitis without hardcoding sepsis or malignancy exclusion.
